sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Postoperative Course
sections.description: This section introduces the patient's medical history, preoperative course, surgical procedure, and the timeline of clinical events leading to the recognition of a significant problem. It establishes the clinical context and sets the stage for understanding why this case presented diagnostic and therapeutic challenges.
subtopics: Patient background: atrial fibrillation, anticoagulation with apixaban, and cardiac findings
Preoperative cardiac catheterization with unfractionated heparin exposure via transradial approach
Cardiac surgery details: coronary artery bypass, aortic valve replacement, ascending aorta replacement with cardiopulmonary bypass
Intraoperative heparin administration (45,000 units) and immediate postoperative hemodynamics
Postoperative timeline: platelet count trajectory from POD1 to POD5, initiation of LMWH thromboprophylaxis
Recognition of progressive thrombocytopenia and discovery of acute cerebral infarct on POD6

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology: Classic HIT versus Autoimmune HIT
sections.description: This section provides the essential pathophysiological foundation needed to understand the case. It explains the mechanisms underlying classic heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and how autoimmune HIT differs, including the molecular basis for the unusual clinical and laboratory features observed in this patient.
subtopics: Classic HIT pathophysiology: PF4-heparin complexes, IgG antibody formation, and FcγRIIa receptor clustering on platelets
The strong prothrombotic nature of HIT: relative risk of thrombosis approximately 15-fold
Typical temporal window for HIT onset after cardiac surgery (POD5-10) and factors influencing timing
Autoimmune HIT (aHIT): heparin-independent platelet-activating properties of antibodies
Mechanism of heparin-independent platelet activation in aHIT
Fc receptor blockade and why aHIT antibodies may show partial resistance to inhibition
Clinical implications of aHIT: more severe thrombocytopenia, persisting hypercoagulability, and treatment challenges

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup and Interpretation of Atypical Laboratory Findings
sections.description: This section details the systematic diagnostic approach used to evaluate the patient's thrombocytopenia. It covers the differential diagnosis, the laboratory investigations performed, and critically analyzes the HIT antibody testing results that revealed an unusual pattern, leading to the diagnosis of autoimmune HIT.
subtopics: Differential diagnosis of post-cardiac surgery thrombocytopenia: cardiogenic shock, infection, post-transfusion purpura, TTP, and drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia
Initial laboratory evaluation: CBC, coagulation profile, haptoglobin, reticulocyte count, and blood cultures
PF4/polyanion ELISA screening: interpretation of strongly positive result (2.2 OD units)
Serotonin-release assay (SRA): principle and typical pattern for classic HIT
Atypical SRA profile in this case: strong serotonin release at 0 U/mL heparin (heparin-independent activation)
Partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade by monoclonal antibody IV.3: significance and interpretation
Diagnostic criteria for aHIT and how this case met them despite initial 'indeterminate' SRA result
Role of early heparin exposure (preoperative cardiac catheterization) in explaining early-onset HIT

sections.description: This section explains the therapeutic decisions made throughout the patient's course, including the rationale for each intervention. It covers the initial anticoagulation changes, the use of high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin, monitoring of consumptive coagulopathy, and the transition between anticoagulant agents based on clinical response.
subtopics: Immediate management: discontinuation of heparin products and LMWH
Argatroban as initial anticoagulant: mechanism as direct thrombin inhibitor, dosing, PTT monitoring, and rationale for selection
High-dose intravenous immunoglobulin: mechanism in aHIT, dosing schedule, and expected versus observed response
Monitoring for HIT-associated consumptive coagulopathy: serial fibrinogen, d-dimer, and schistocyte detection
Recognition of inadequate anticoagulation control: falling fibrinogen, rising d-dimer, and persistent schistocytes
Transition to fondaparinux: rationale, mechanism as antithrombin-dependent factor Xa inhibitor, and antithrombin supplementation
Long-term anticoagulation: resumption of apixaban after platelet count recovery

sections.description: This section describes the patient's recovery trajectory and synthesizes the important clinical and laboratory lessons from this case. It emphasizes the novel aspects of the case and provides practical guidance for clinicians who may encounter similar patients.
subtopics: Platelet count recovery timeline: gradual improvement to normal by POD62
Complete neurological recovery and functional outcome
Serial SRA testing: evolution of antibody profile from aHIT pattern to classic HIT pattern over months
Novel aspects of this case: early postoperative onset, profound thrombocytopenia nadir (13×10⁹/L), and partial Fc receptor blockade resistance
Clinical pearl: preoperative heparin exposure can lead to early-onset HIT/aHIT before POD5
Clinical pearl: atypical or 'indeterminate' SRA results should raise suspicion for aHIT
Clinical pearl: partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade indicates unusually reactive aHIT antibodies
Importance of considering aHIT in the differential diagnosis of severe, persistent thrombocytopenia with thrombosis after heparin exposure
